story: On Magnolia Loop in Sumter Oaks, this sunny Sunday afternoon at 79 degrees, Rosa has been named the parade committee's lead, and Donna is already eager to launch the sign-up sheet on the bulletin board. Gary, optimistic as ever, promises to sketch out the wiring and lights for all four golf carts so they can be bolted on the moment the board approves. Hal grudgingly signs on as the committee's decoration inspector, notebook in pocket, insisting that three flamingos and a garaged cart are about as much excitement as he can allow.

gary.thought_process: Rosa and Donna are planning the parade, Hal is counting flamingos, and everyone knows the cart is parked until Architectural Review signs off. I've said my piece to Hal already, so no need to repeat it. What I can do that's useful is something that feels like me: tell Rosa I'm in for the parade and offer to handle the wiring and lights design on paper, so everything's ready the moment the board approves. That keeps me legal, useful, and part of the group.

parameters.content: Count me in for the parade, Rosa. I'll draw up the wiring plan and lights for all four carts on paper while we wait on the board, so we can bolt it all on the minute they sign off.

donna.thought_process: The cart situation is settled and everyone's talking parade, which is my kind of project. Rosa wants all four of us on the Loop with decorated carts, and I just said I'd chair the committee, so now I should get it organized instead of repeating myself. Gary's cart stays in the garage until Architectural Review signs off, so the plan has to work around that. Hal's busy counting my flamingos, so I'll keep him in the loop by giving him a job. Tomorrow's nine o'clock practice is already set with Gary, so nothing more to say there. Time to assign roles and get the committee moving.

parameters.content: Rosa, committee's official! You pick the theme and I'll make a sign-up sheet for the bulletin board. Hal can be our compliance officer, he's already counting, so everything we hang stays within the rules and Gary's cart rides only once it's approved.

hal.thought_process: Gary says his cart application is filed and the cart stays garaged, and Rosa says it's settled. Donna counted her flamingos at three, which is the legal limit, so there's nothing for me to report on either front. My notebook has nothing to add today. Rosa is asking for help with the Halloween parade, and I like order and respect, which a well-run parade has plenty of. I'll put the notebook away, join in, and offer to keep the decorations and cart entries within the rules so no one gets a violation. Might as well be useful. I'm not about to say I'm soft on any of them.

parameters.content: Fine, notebook's going in my pocket. Three flamingos and a garaged cart suit me. I'll help with the parade, but somebody has to keep the decorations legal, and I volunteer.

rosa.thought_process: Hal is counting Donna's flamingos for his notebook, Gary has said his piece on the cart, and Donna signed on to chair the parade committee. My real goal is the Halloween parade with all four of us on decorated carts, and I've already told Hal to put the notebook away. Nobody's asked me anything new, so I shouldn't re-ask or repeat myself. The useful next step is to give the committee a concrete job: Halloween decorating is allowed all week, and Donna's flamingos sit right at the L-02 limit of three. I'll bring that to Donna and Hal together, since Hal's count is the thing he'll care about, and assign him a task to turn his notebook into something helpful.

parameters.content: Madam chair, first job: Hal's already counting your flamingos, so let's make him the committee's official decoration inspector. Keep every porch at three or fewer ornaments from the street, and we'll never give him a line to write.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
